title: Roos fibres preserve cones, shifts and levelwise quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $R$ a sheaf of rings on the pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use cochain complexes and cones of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a strict inverse tower $N=(N_n,t_n)_{n\ge1}$ of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-inverse-system], let $P(N)=\prod_nN_n$ be the termwise product [def-weil-category-product], let $s_N=1-T_N$ with $\operatorname{pr}_nT_N=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$, and set $H(N)=\operatorname{Cone}(s_N)[-1]$. In reordered coordinates,
$$H(N)^q=P(N)^q\oplus P(N)^{q-1},\qquad d(v,u)=(dv,-du-s_Nv).$$
On strict tower maps let $H$ act diagonally by the product map. This is an additive functor, it sends levelwise quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and its localized Roos triangle makes $QH(N)$ a derived limit of $(QN_n)_n$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. For every strict tower map $f:N\to N'$ there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(H(f)),\qquad(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(b,b',a,-a'),$$
in source order $P(N')^q,P(N)^{q+1},P(N')^{q-1},P(N)^q$. It preserves the cone inclusion and boundary after the shift comparison. The coherent natural shift comparison $H(N[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(N)[r]$ is $(v,u)\mapsto(v,(-1)^r u)$. If $j_n:M\to N_n$ are compatible chain maps, $m\mapsto((j_n(m))_n,0)$ is a natural chain map $M\to H(N)$. The cone and shift comparisons carry such zero-second-coordinate augmentations to the induced cone and shifted augmentations whenever the levelwise augmentations do so.

source.place: Cones paragraph, Roos-fibre sentence and cone/shift commutation sentence. Supporting sources: Stacks Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit) and Tag 07KC (lemma-products).

proof.text: All coordinates below denote biproduct components, so the calculations are identities of morphisms of module sheaves. Termwise products exist by [det-pe-products-exact]. The product universal property [def-weil-category-product] defines $T_N$ and gives $dT_N=T_Nd$, since each $t_n$ is a chain map. Hence $s_N=1-T_N$ is a chain map. The cone and shift definitions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give the stated reordered differential; its square is $(0,(ds_N-s_Nd)v)=0$. For a strict map $f:N\to N'$, put $F=P(f)$. The compatibility in [def-weil-inverse-system], checked after each projection, gives $Fs_N=s_{N'}F$. Consequently $\operatorname{diag}(F,F)$ commutes with the displayed differential. Products preserve identities, composition and addition of maps because these equations hold after every projection. The diagonal formula therefore defines the asserted additive functor $H$.

source.place: Cones paragraph, functorial termwise fibre construction; expanded coordinate verification

proof.text: Exact countable products from [det-pe-products-exact] imply that the strict product map P(f) of levelwise quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism, because homology preserves exact products: the natural product comparison conjugates the induced homology map to the product of the levelwise homology isomorphisms. Form the commuting-square morphism of the mapping-cone triangles of roosU(N) and roosU(N′). After localization, its first two maps are isomorphisms, so the triangulated two-out-of-three lemma gives an isomorphism on cones [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Reflect isomorphisms through Q and shift by -1 [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to obtain the quasi-isomorphism roosF.map f. This avoids a second coordinate comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 07KC (exact products); mapping-cone triangle comparison by triangulated two-out-of-three and shift invariance.

proof.text: Use [det-pe-products-exact] to give the module category CountableAB4Star. Apply [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core] to the evaluated strict tower: its actual termwise product cone, with actual localized projections, is limiting. Its unique product isomorphism e to the chosen product in the derived category conjugates Q(roosU N) to the derived transition endomorphism, as checked after every projection. The library mapping-cocone triangle is distinguished [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-triangulated-category]. Transport its two product vertices by e. The resulting distinguished triangle satisfies [def-weil-derived-limit], with first map Q(roosProj N) followed by e and last map e.inv followed by the localized cocone boundary.

proof.text: Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and write $\epsilon=(-1)^r$. Under the termwise product identification $P(N[r])=P(N)[r]$, the differential of $H(N[r])$ is $(\epsilon dv,-\epsilon du-s_Nv)$ and that of $H(N)[r]$ is $(\epsilon dv,-\epsilon du-\epsilon s_Nv)$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The map $\sigma_{N,r}(v,u)=(v,\epsilon u)$ has inverse with the same formula. Both $\sigma d$ and $d\sigma$ equal $(\epsilon dv,-du-\epsilon s_Nv)$, so it is a chain isomorphism. It commutes with diagonal product maps, proving naturality. For $r=0$ it is the identity, and applying the comparisons for $r$ and $s$ successively multiplies the second coordinate by $(-1)^r(-1)^s=(-1)^{r+s}$. This proves coherence under the usual reindexing of iterated shifts. The product identifications here are the unique projection-preserving ones of [def-weil-category-product]. In Lean, [lem-weil-product-comm-shift] constructs the unique projection-preserving product comparison, the one-minus-transition natural transformation commutes with it projectionwise, and [lem-weil-signed-mapping-cocone-shift] supplies the signed coherent cocone shift. The homotopy-cofiber arrow map agrees with the existing mappingCone.map by its two inclusions, giving the natural identity-component isomorphism to roosF. The two cocone inclusions then prove precisely ShiftFormula.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; explicit Roos calculation required by the blueprint Cones paragraph

proof.text:
For a strict tower map $f:N\to N'$, write $A=P(N)$, $B=P(N')$, $F=P(f)$, $S_A=s_N$ and $S_B=s_{N'}$. Products of the two summands in $\operatorname{Cone}(f_n)^q$ identify $P(\operatorname{Cone}(f))^q=B^q\oplus A^{q+1}$: the map takes the two component projections, and its inverse pairs them at each $n$; their composites are identities after each product projection [def-weil-category-product]. The cone differential is $(b,a)\mapsto(db+Fa,-da)$ and its transition endomorphism is $\operatorname{diag}(S_B,S_A)$. Consequently the differential on $H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ is
$$D(b,a,b',a')=(db+Fa,-da,-db'-Fa'-S_Bb,da'-S_Aa).$$
The cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives
$$D'(b,b',a,c)=(db+Fa,-db'-S_Bb+Fc,-da,dc+S_Aa)$$
on $\operatorname{Cone}(H(f))$. Hence $\Phi(b,a,b',a')=(b,b',a,-a')$ satisfies $\Phi D=D'\Phi$, both sides being $(db+Fa,-db'-Fa'-S_Bb,-da,-da'+S_Aa)$. Its inverse is $(b,b',a,c)\mapsto(b,a,b',-c)$. This proves the asserted chain isomorphism without invoking an unstated commutation-of-cones lemma.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; explicit double-cone calculation for the blueprint Cones paragraph

proof.text: A strict commutative square between $f$ and $g$, with maps $\alpha$ on the sources and $\beta$ on the targets, acts on the four source coordinates as $(P\beta,P\alpha,P\beta,P\alpha)$. On the reordered target coordinates it acts as $(P\beta,P\beta,P\alpha,P\alpha)$. Permutation and multiplication by $-1$ commute with these maps; thus $\Phi$ is natural. The cone inclusion sends $(b,b')$ to $(b,0,b',0)$ before $\Phi$, and to $(b,b',0,0)$ afterwards, exactly the cone inclusion for $H(f)$. For the cone boundary convention $-p$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $H(-p)$ sends $(b,a,b',a')$ to $(-a,-a')$ in $H(N[1])$. The shift comparison of step 4 sends this to $(-a,a')$ in $H(N)[1]$, exactly $-p\Phi$. This proves preservation of the boundary after the shift comparison, including its sign.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and Tag 014Q, definition-distinguished-triangle (cone boundary -p)

proof.text: Given compatible $j_n:M\to N_n$, define $J:M\to P(N)$ by the product universal property [def-weil-category-product]. Since $t_nj_{n+1}=j_n$, every projection of $s_NJ$ is zero, so $s_NJ=0$. Hence $d(Jm,0)=(Jdm,0)$, proving that $\eta_j:m\mapsto(Jm,0)$ is a chain map by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $g:M\to M'$ and a strict $f:N\to N'$ satisfy $f_nj_n=j'_ng$, then $P(f)J=J'g$ after every projection. The diagonal formula for $H(f)$ now gives $H(f)\eta_j=\eta_{j'}g$. This is the asserted naturality of the augmentation.

source.place: Cones paragraph, canonical maps to the strict Roos model; explicit zero-second-coordinate lift

proof.text: For shifted augmentations, $\sigma_{N,r}\eta_{j[r]}$ and $\eta_j[r]$ both send $m$ to $(Jm,0)$ after reindexing, because $(-1)^r0=0$. For cone augmentations, let $g:M\to M'$ and $f:N\to N'$ satisfy $f_nj_n=j'_ng$. The induced levelwise cone map sends $(m',m)$ to $(j'_nm',j_nm)$ by the cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its zero-second-coordinate augmentation to $H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ is $((J'm',Jm),(0,0))$. Step 5 sends this to $((J'm',0),(Jm,0))$, exactly the cone map induced by $\eta_{j'}$ and $\eta_j$. Together with the inclusion and boundary identities of step 6, this proves the final augmentation compatibility for cones and shifts. All calculations are identities of the specified maps, rather than choices of morphisms completing triangulated diagrams.
